evidence: Panel A: I-10 runs vertically (NW-SE) as a wide divided freeway; Queen Creek Rd / SR 347 crosses it horizontally on a single grade-separated crossing.

Panel A: four diagonal one-way ramps, one per quadrant, meet the cross street at two separate at-grade junctions, one on each side of the freeway; no loop ramps and no crossovers between the junctions.

Panel A: the two ramp junctions sit well outside the freeway edges with the cross street running conventionally (right side) between them, which matches a conventional diamond rather than a tight diamond, SPUI or DDI.
Panel B / tables: freeway links 101-106 on two carriageways (x=-60 SE-bound, x=+60 NW-bound); ramps 301-304 each connect one merge_diverge node (11-14) to one terminal port.
Panel B / tables: arterial boundary nodes 1,2 at x=-600 and 3,4 at x=+600; eastbound on y=-22 (201, 205, 204), westbound on y=+22 (203, 206, 202).

Panel B / tables: west terminal (ports 21-26, x=-320..-210) has 6 connectors 401-406; east terminal (ports 31-36, x=210..320) has 6 connectors 411-416; 205 and 206 are the arterial links between the terminals.

Local axes: +x is NE along Queen Creek Rd, so the west terminal is the SW terminal and the east terminal is the NE terminal; both terminal centroids lie on y=0, the C/D grid line, and are assigned to row D.
